title: Mark Clattenburg apologises over Vinicius Jr comments during Real Madrid vs. Benfica
content:
Former Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg has apologised after saying Vinicius Junior “has not helped himself” as the forward alleged he was racially abused during Real Madrid’s win over Benfica on Tuesday.

Play was stopped for around eight minutes after the incident, following the Brazil international’s opening goal and yellow card after his celebration. During this time Vinicius Jr appeared to point at Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni, after which referee Francois Letexier initiated alleged racial abuse protocol by crossing his wrists.

Clattenburg said on commentary for Amazon Prime that Vinicius Jr “has made this difficult for the referee”, adding that “all he has to do – yes, celebrate – is return back” but he “has not helped himself”. These comments drew criticism over social media, with former player Troy Townsend saying “he should never be involved in commentary ever again”.

Clattenburg released a statement on Wednesday saying “nothing justifies racism in sport or in life”.

“I’m grateful to have a chance to follow-up on last night, I got it wrong, I’m sorry,” he added. “It was live TV, my job is to respond in the moment and the words I used were clumsy and not right.

“I’m already learning from this and appreciate my colleagues who covered the situation with class throughout.”

On Wednesday, UEFA announced it had opened an investigation into Vinicius Jr’s allegations of racial abuse. An investigation, however, is expected to take weeks meaning Prestianni will likely be available for the second leg in Madrid next Wednesday. Vinicius Jr’s team-mate, Kylian Mbappe, alleged that he had heard Prestianni “say that Vinicius is a monkey, five times”. Prestianni, 20, denied the allegation of racism in an Instagram post.

Immediately after the game, Benfica coach Jose Mourinho accused Vinicius Jr of inciting the incident. The 63-year-old Portuguese said he had reminded the forward that “the biggest person in the history of (Benfica)” — referring to their legendary forward Eusebio — “is Black” and said that “every stadium where Vinicius plays, something happens”.

These comments were criticised by Clarence Seedorf on Amazon Prime, while Thierry Henry accused Mourinho of trying to deflect.

Benfica said in a social media post after the match, alongside an attached video of the alleged incident: “As the images demonstrate, given the distance, the Real Madrid players could not have heard what they claim to have heard.”

Vinicius Jr, who has suffered several incidents of racist abuse at stadiums in Spain, posted on Instagram about the incident later on Tuesday night, saying: “Racists are, above all, cowards. They need to put their shirts over their mouths to show how weak they are.”

Madrid will face Benfica in the second leg of the play-off tie at the Bernabeu on February 25.
